answer: Persistent Attention Ledger: each identity must hold a rotating gale of small, unpredictable response duties across many periods, verified by peers. Missed duties trigger a prism check that splits reputation across all prior periods, revealing inactivity. New identities need a comet of continuous, costly participation—roughly 40 hours of verified low-latency replies—before earning any weight. Sybils pay that attention cost per fake identity, and parallelism is capped, making mass fabrication economically ruinous.
